title: How efficient is an electric kettle?
examples: Where does wasted energy go in a kettle?

outputs.label: Heats kettle body
outputs.ask: Where does the wasted energy go?

explain.say: When you switch on a kettle for tea or noodles, you pay for the electricity. But does all of it heat the water? Not quite! Let us follow every bit of energy and see where it goes. This picture is called a Sankey diagram.

draw.text: How efficient is an electric kettle?

outputs.label: Heats kettle body
outputs.ask: Where does the wasted energy go?

explain.say: Look at the thick arrow going straight on: heating the water. That is the useful part, about 90 out of every 100 joules. Useful means it does the job we want. How much of the energy is useful?

outputs.label: Heats kettle body
outputs.ask: Where does the wasted energy go?

explain.say: About 90 percent, yes! Now look at the thin arrows bending away. Some energy warms the kettle's own body, some escapes into the air. That is wasted energy, which means it spreads out where we do not want it. Which wasted arrow is biggest?

outputs.label: Heats kettle body
outputs.ask: Where does the wasted energy go?

explain.say: Heating the kettle body, at 6 percent. There is even a tiny bit of sound, that rumble as it boils. Efficiency is useful energy out divided by total energy in: 90 divided by 100, so 0.9, or 90 percent. Can energy ever be more than 100 percent efficient?

outputs.label: Heats kettle body
outputs.ask: Where does the wasted energy go?

explain.say: Never, great thinking! Energy cannot be created. Kettles are among the most efficient machines at home. Wow fact: an old filament bulb was only about 5 percent efficient; the rest was heat. Challenge: how could you make a kettle waste even less energy?

outputs.label: Heats kettle body
outputs.ask: Where does the wasted energy go?

faq.a: Efficiency equals useful energy out divided by total energy in. Multiply by 100 to get a percentage.

faq.q: Where does the wasted energy go?
faq.a: It heats the kettle, the worktop and the air, and a little becomes sound. It spreads out into the surroundings.
asks: Where does wasted energy go in a kettle?

faq.a: A Sankey diagram shows energy flow with arrows whose widths match the amounts. Useful energy goes straight on, and wasted energy bends away.
asks: How do you draw a Sankey diagram?

faq.a: Almost nothing is, because some energy is always wasted as heat or sound. More than 100 percent is impossible, as energy cannot be created.

faq.q: How can a kettle waste less energy?
faq.a: Boil only the water you need, keep the kettle free of limescale and use an insulated kettle so less heat escapes.
asks: How do I save energy with a kettle?

facts: Efficiency = useful energy output ÷ total energy input (× 100 for a percentage).
Electric kettles typically transfer about 80–90% of their electrical energy to the water.

quiz.say: A motor takes in 200 J and gives 150 J of useful energy. Efficiency?
quiz.show: A motor takes in 200 J and gives 150 J of useful energy. Efficiency?

wrong.0: That divides input by output; efficiency can never be over 100%.
wrong.1: That uses the wasted 50 J; use the useful 150 J.

quiz.say: In a Sankey diagram, what does a wider arrow mean?
quiz.show: In a Sankey diagram, what does a wider arrow mean?
quiz.why: Arrow width is drawn in proportion to the amount of energy.

wrong.2: Width shows how much energy, not temperature.
